title: Question About Sergio Leone's 'Once Upon a Time' and 'Dollars' Trilogies

commenti.body: They are not connected at all. You should watch the Dollars trilogy in order if you can, mostly just to avoid disappointment since the first one is easily the weakest. But I am loath to even accept that Once Upon a Time is a trilogy at all or in any sense. Chronologically, geographically, thematically, characteristically, they have nothing to do with each other. They're not even in the same genre.
more of a naming convention than anything else.

>But I am loath to even accept that Once Upon a Time is a trilogy at all or in any sense.

Leone has said they cover three periods in American history that he found interesting. That way they have some kind of connection.

At the end of the day both so called trilogies have movies with no narrative connection at all.  The three with Eastwood do have him as the common factor but in every movie he plays another character.

In short, no. None of them are connected, not even the Dollars Trilogy.

The three “Dollars” films were all made individually, and only shared Clint Eastwood as the main character. His character has a different name in all three films.

But, as was often the case in the ‘60s, foreign films didn’t get released in America the year they came out in Europe… there were often big delays. So it was only once The Good, the Bad and the Ugly came out that distributors packaged them as a “trilogy” and sold them for American exhibition. Which lead to them unofficially being called a trilogy, even though they weren’t connected.

The other three films have nothing to do with each other. Duck You Sucker was not even meant to be directed by Leone… he took over the reigns very late in the pre-production due to some issues with the original director (which is why I’d say it’s easily the least interesting of his films).

And Once Upon a Time in America just reused the “Once Upon a Time…” name in order to help get financing off the back of the success of West. Leone had lots of trouble later in his career getting films made, because his visions kept getting more and more epic and yet they were still arthouse films.

There’s actually some super interesting stories out there about the films he couldn’t get made before his death, including “Leningrad”, which was intended to open with the most ambitious shot of his entire career.

The only advice I can give here is to save Once Upon A Time in the West for last. At least as far as westerns go. If you are just beginning to watch westerns this is really a great end cap to western the genre which was becoming less popular by the late 60s. This plays wonderful homage to all the westerns that came before. It’s one of my favorite movies and it’s really spectacular and you will benefit having watched earlier westerns.
I'm aware but I still think his seeing so is tenuous at best, downright schizophrenic at worst

The 'Once Upon a Time' trilogy is unofficial, it's not a real trilogy per se. Even the Dollars Trilogy isn't exactly official, though it's more widely accepted as one in popular culture than the other three films because Clint Eastwood at least plays a similar character in each of the films.

I've never heard of the 'Once Upon' trilogy, seems tenuous to me. The Dollars trilogy shares a a similar protagonist played by Eastwood, in the same genre, so that makes perfect sense enough to comprise that trilogy.

Leone, who only wanted to supervise the film, took over the directing reins of *Duck You Sucker* from his regular assistant director Santi less than 2 weeks into production because Rod Steiger decided he only want to be directed Leone himself.  Santi shifted over to doing 2nd unit.
Once Upon a Time in the West and Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid are perfect codas for the genre.

I don't know why everyone is saying the Dollars/Man with No Name movies aren't related. It's true that some actors play different roles throughout the films, but the main character, played by Eastwood is the same character. The movies actually take place in reverse chronological order of release but I wouldn't recommend watching them that way. You can tell the continuity by several clues, but the the biggest is >!his clothes and in particular the condition of his hat.!< Fistfull of Dollars 1964) is based on the same story as the samurai classic Yojimbo (1961), who's main character also only goes by a nickname, 30 year old mullbery field (Sanjuro Kuwabatake), and indeed has a different nickname in his next film, Sanjuro (1962), 30 year old camellia (plant).
I despise Once upon a time in AMerica.  I waited decades to see the film, saving it for a rainy day and it sucked, really sucked.  I felt sorry for Elizabeth Mcgovern.
The Good, The Bad and The Ugly is a screech, but the first and second are definitely related

There is no Once Upon a Time Trilogy. Once Upon a Time in the West was supposed to be another Eastwood vehicle but he turned it down. Leone had to settle for Charles Bronson. The Dollars trilogy would have been a quadrilogy with Eastwood. That film still feels more connected to the Dollars films than anything that came after.

Dollars trilogy are just 3 separate movies with a similar character played by Clint… but also, some people interpret Good, Bad, Ugly as a prequel to the others because of some of his wardrobe acquisitions in that film.

Also Lee Van Cleef is in Few Dollars More and GBU, but he’s two different characters.

No connection between stories, just same actors in the dollars trilogy but not chatacters. The only connections are in style and a few elements and topics of the plot. 
Leone is really one of the greatest directors in cinema history, but unluckily not a prolific one, he directed just 7 movies.
Well, Once Upon a Time in America counts as two films in one! 
The same for Once Upon in the West! 
Lol! 
I suggest to watch his movies from the first to the last to see the evolution of his style!
